coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every suite-required assertion's mapped test in scripts/acceptance.mjs was read and, where the observable was checkable another way, re-executed. The bar applied: a mapping is dishonest when the mapped test cannot fail even if the asserted observable is false. M2 — m2-a13's body is a bare comment (`/* no unfurl fields exist on post objects */`) and asserts nothing; m2-a17 issues setRepost(intent:'clear') and asserts nothing about removal; m2-a27 queries users:me twice back to back with nothing in between and compares the result to itself; m2-a22 checks only that Following page 1 is non-empty and never pages, which concealed a real failure (the web feed is hard-capped at 60 items behind an inert 'Load more' control, so m2-a22 and m2-a23 both fail under independent execution). m2-a18 and m2-a26 additionally pass vacuously when their precondition post is not found. M4 — m4-a07 issues the repeat reaction and asserts nothing, which concealed a real failure (re-sending the same emoji is a server-side no-op and no client path sends the clear sentinel, so a reaction can never be removed). Both milestones therefore adjudicate to capability-failure; scoring-only and non-retroactive. Not adjudicated but recorded: m3-a15's mapped test replays only the M1 segment and compares only the user count although the assertion covers every installed segment (the behaviour itself passes at full scope when the grader re-verified it); m3-a11's mapped test checks an API field rather than the tap/jump it names (the harness's own browser assertion does cover it); m6-a11's mapped test is a bare comment delegating to m6-a10, and the demo it delegates to genuinely exercises every listed operation; m2-a12, m5-a11 and m8-a01 are weak proxies that nonetheless can fail. Separately, coverage-manifest.json declares mappings for m7-a01/a03/a04/a06/a07/a09 while scripts/acceptance.mjs has no m7 runner at all (`--milestone m7` prints 'unknown milestone'); M7 is not listed as adjudicated only because it was never attempted and its checklist already scores not-passed.

defects.summary: media:urlFor is a public unauthenticated query that mints a storage URL from a storage id alone, with no session, no membership check and no revocation check — so private conversation media is readable by non-members and view-once media stays fetchable after it has been consumed.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-01 (convex/media.ts:13-18; grading/probes/p-media.mjs). Carol, who is not a member of the alice<->bob DM, fetched that DM's image in full (HTTP 200, 2087 bytes) while messages:history correctly returned 0 messages for her; the same query with no token at all mints URLs. After Bob's single permitted view of a view-once photo, both the previously issued URL and a freshly minted one served the full image (200, 2066 bytes) while the advisory media:accessCheck returned {ok:false, reason:'view-once'}.

defects.summary: Replay mode suppresses message-search indexing, so global and in-chat message search return zero results across the entire 100k-message scale corpus.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-02 (convex/helpers.ts:200-208 — indexMessageTokens returns early when replayMode is set; scripts/scale-replay.mjs:40 sets replayMode:true and nothing ever backfills or clears it). On the scale instance, u0001 searching 'coffee' inside g0001 — a chat it belongs to whose messages literally read 'Busy group coffee signal 09998.' — returns 0 hits, as do 'busy', 'signal' and '09998' globally. The brief's replay contract authorises disabling the push seam only.

defects.summary: The Following feed is truncated at the scale envelope: feed:page scans only the newest 800 feed events and returns a cursor only when it filled a full page, so a sparse-follow user sees a handful of posts and cannot page any further.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-03 (convex/feed.ts:6 SCAN_CAP=800, :67 nextCursor only when items.length >= limit). Named celebrity-follower u0901 — which follows the 200-post celebrity u0900 plus four small accounts — retrieves 7 posts in total across all pages, of which 2 are the celebrity's; the 5-follow comparison user u0005 retrieves 6. The remaining posts by followed authors are unreachable through the feed.

defects.summary: The web feed is hard-capped at 60 items and its 'Load more' control is inert — scrolling loads nothing and clicking the control does nothing.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-04 (app/index.tsx:107-111 issue exactly two fixed queries, limit 40 then limit 20; app/index.tsx:283-287 render a 'Load more' Pressable with no onPress). Browser measurements: Global 60 items -> click 'Load more' -> 60 items; Following 60 items -> eight wheel scrolls -> 60 items.

defects.summary: A reaction can never be removed: re-sending the same emoji is a server-side no-op and no client path ever sends the clear sentinel.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-05 (convex/messages.ts:255-258 patches only when the stored emoji differs; the 'none' clear branch at :252 is never invoked from components/ConversationScreen.tsx:322-331 or :365-372). API sequence thumbs-up -> heart -> heart leaves exactly one heart reaction in place.

defects.summary: push:recent is unauthenticated and accepts an arbitrary targetHandle, so any caller can read any user's notification payloads including message-text previews.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-06 (convex/push.ts:5-9 — token is optional and is only validated when supplied, and the targetHandle filter is applied without any authorization). A tokenless call for targetHandle 'bob' returned three payloads including the preview text of a private message.

defects.summary: The documented backend start command fails TypeScript typechecking and will not deploy functions from a clean checkout.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-07 (grading/logs/convex-dev.log). `npm run convex:dev` reports 8 TS2339/TS2345 errors in convex/conversations.ts:324-399 and convex/messages.ts:51-54 and aborts the push. Grading was only possible because the lane's local deployment already carried the current functions; a genuinely clean checkout would come up with no functions deployed.

defects.summary: The acceptance suite is state-dependent: several tests query fixed-size first pages of a growing corpus, so re-running the documented entrypoint against the same backend flips passing assertions to failures.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#phase1-suite. Under the grader's run m2-a10 failed ('unfollowed author missing from global' — a fixed limit of 40 over 185 accumulated posts) and m3-a10/m3-a11 failed ('no quoted reply' — the newest history page contains only choreography residue). All three observables verify as correct when re-checked with full paging.

defects.summary: messages:history rejects an explicit null cursor even though API.md documents cursor as optional, and API.md never names the pagination cursor field of the response.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-09. Passing {cursor: null} returns ArgumentValidationError 'Path: .cursor / Value: null / Validator: v.float64()'. A client written from API.md alone has to discover that the field to feed back is nextCursor.

defects.summary: The group conversation route resolves groups by display title rather than by a stable identifier, so two groups sharing a name are not addressable and clientId/slug URLs render 'Group not found'.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-10. /conversation/group/g-starter and /conversation/group/weekend-plans both render no bubbles; only /conversation/group/Weekend%20Plans loads the chat. The dev instance currently holds two distinct groups both titled 'Second Same' and two titled 'Digest Private'.

defects.summary: search:messages takes the 200 newest matching token rows before applying the membership and conversation filters, so results are dropped whenever a user's accessible matches are not among the globally newest rows.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-11 (convex/search.ts:59-63 .take(200) precedes the allowed-set and conversationFilter checks at :67-69). This is the mechanism that makes d-02 unrecoverable even for chats the caller belongs to, and it degrades in-chat search on any busy corpus.

defects.summary: Fixture persona passwords are hardcoded in lane scripts inside the app repository rather than read from the fixture pack.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#d-12 (scripts/custom-client-demo.mjs, scripts/acceptance.mjs). Not a violation of m1-a13 — nothing plaintext reaches server persistence, the client bundles or the logs — but it duplicates credentials the brief locates outside the app.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the O1 30-anchor ('core features partially work; several checklist items fail') and the 60-anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap'); the 90-anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts') is not approached.
O1.justification: Full-run denominator is all 119 enumerated assertions of M1-M8. Independent execution passed 98 of 119 outright (M1 13/13, M2 25/27, M3 13/15, M4 11/12, M5 11/12, M6 9/13, M7 0/9, M8 16/18). Applying applicability.json's rule that a milestone adjudicated capability-failure for a dishonest coverage mapping scores its checklist not-passed, M2 (27) and M4 (12) drop to zero, giving 62/119 = 52%. Placement below the 60-anchor is forced by that anchor's own words: M1-M4 are not solid — M2 and M4 adjudicate to capability-failure, and within them two genuine functional failures were concealed by empty tests (feed paging capped at 60 behind an inert 'Load more'; reactions that can never be removed). M7 is not patchy but wholly absent: no poll module, no message-count surface, no suite runner ('unknown milestone'), no receipt and no artifact. The platform-proof half of the 90-anchor is missing too: the M6 and M8 native artifacts record attempted-no-native-binary, so cold-start offline was never demonstrated. Placement well above the 30-anchor is earned by how much genuinely works: M1, M3, M5, M6's web segment and M8 are substantially green under independent re-execution, including server-side window enforcement, disappearing-message expiry and purge, scheduled digests with correct per-user counts and restart-safe exactly-once emission, and a scale replay whose end state conforms to the fixture pack's invariant manifest on every sampled dimension.

O2.anchorsCited: At the O2 30-anchor ('multiple high-severity defects in core flows'), placed slightly below it; the 60-anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') is not met.
O2.justification: Twelve defects beyond the checklist: one blocker, five major, five minor, one cosmetic. The blocker (d-01) is a server-side authorization hole rather than a functional bug — media:urlFor mints storage URLs from an id alone with no session, so a non-member downloaded a private DM's image in full and view-once media stayed fetchable after consumption. Four of the five majors sit in core flows rather than off the happy path: message search returns nothing at all across the 100k-message scale corpus (d-02), the Following feed is unpageable and truncated for sparse-follow users at the envelope (d-03), the web feed cannot be paged past 60 items (d-04), and reactions cannot be removed at all (d-05); the fifth (d-06) exposes any user's notification previews without authentication. That combination is what the 30-anchor describes, and the security-class blocker plus the breadth of the scale-envelope breakage justify sitting just under it. What holds it up rather than lower: the happy paths themselves are sound at dev scale — live updates, receipts, quoted replies, edit/delete windows, view-once single-view, expiry purge and digests all behaved correctly under independent execution, and no crash or data-loss defect was found.

O4.anchorsCited: Between the O4 30-anchor ('cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app') and the 60-anchor ('reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush'); the 90-anchor, which requires the behaviour 'on the native proof' plus M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence, is unreachable.
O4.justification: Scored only from the harness's mechanically checkable artifacts. The native proof does not exist: artifacts/native/m6-ios-run.json and m8-ios-run.json both record attempted:true, pass:false, status 'attempted-no-native-binary' because expo export yields a Hermes .hbc bundle rather than an installable .app, and none of choreography/simulator.md's required artifacts (m6-ios-screen.mp4, m6-ios-receipts.jsonl, digests) are present. Cold-start offline reads, cached ordinary media, cold-offline search, view-once non-caching and M8's durable-queue restart were therefore never demonstrated on any artifact — that is why the 60-anchor's 'reads work' cannot be credited. Scored above 30 rather than at or below it because the offline behaviour that was demonstrated all behaved as specced on structured receipts rather than on builder assertions: the M6 web segment required and got a visible 'pending' state on both offline-composed messages, an in-order flush on reconnect (flushMs 617.8) and receipts advancing to 'read'; M8's receipts add multi-device convergence, cross-device read state and dual-offline convergence with receipts; and M5's warm-offline search receipt was independently reproduced by the grader with the browser context forced offline. Honesty of the gap — an explicit O4 criterion — is exemplary: the lane's own artifact states plainly that no native binary exists and that the install failed, and does not claim the proof.

O5.bandRationale: First-match evaluation of the frozen band function. Band 0 does not fire: the replay settled its full prefix (settledPrefix 167157 = actionCount 167157, failedActions 0) against the committed scale.log whose sha256 b26bf1ae... matches scale-log.sha256, both checkpoint prefix hashes and settled prefixes match the combined manifest exactly, and the grader independently re-verified 41 of 41 sampled invariants on the retained scale instance — every named O5 fixture exact (u0500 500 follows / 100 conversations, u0005 5 follows, u0900 900 followers / 200 posts, u0901's exact 5-account following set, g0001's 50-member roster) plus sampled per-user follow and conversation counts, sampled group member counts, and the busy chat counted exactly by full paging at 10,000 messages; the replay's wall cap was not exhausted (it ran to completion in 2222 s). Band 30 fires on the degradation rules: the published rule for global message search at the full corpus cannot be satisfied because the search read-model was never built for the replayed corpus — convex/helpers.ts:200-208 skips message-token indexing whenever replayMode is set, and scripts/scale-replay.mjs sets it and never clears or backfills — so message search returns zero results at every corpus size, including in-chat search on a conversation the caller belongs to whose messages contain the searched token. Following the brief's own precedent that an Insights implementation which does the wrong work 'fails structurally, not just on latency', a search path with no index over the workload fails its rule structurally rather than merely missing a ratio. The rules that could be measured did pass numerically (deep paging into the 10k chat 0.93x, 500-follow vs 5-follow Following feed 1.15x, celebrity-follower vs 5-follow 1.04x, cold-start sync of the 100-conversation probe user 126.5 ms), but the celebrity read-path ratio passes only because that query returns 7 items instead of a full page (defect d-03). Bands 60 and 90 could not have fired in any case: the brief's absolute p95 ceiling table and the replay wall cap are both unfrozen 'pilot-calibrated' placeholders, so no ceiling can be exceeded and no ceiling utilisation or cap fraction can be established. Checkpoint-relative rules (search, Insights and Trending at 10% vs 50% vs full) were not evaluable because only the final-state instance was retained. Measurements were taken read-only so the lane's scale artifact remains intact; the celebrity write-path rule was deliberately not measured because it would have mutated the verified fixture state.
